canonicalIngredients.name: pork shoulder
observations: 600 g pork scotch fillet / butt, 2 cm pieces (s1)
1.5 lb pork butt or shoulder, 1 inch cubes, fat trimmed (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: cornflour
observations: 60 g / 1/2 cup in batter + 1 tbsp sauce slurry (s1)
1 tbsp in marinade + 1/2 cup dredge, optional slurry (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: soy sauce
observations: 1 tbsp in marinade + 1 tbsp in sauce (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: vinegar
observations: 80 ml apple cider or rice wine (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: pineapple
observations: 95 g / 1/2 cup canned chunks in juice, drained (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: pineapple juice
observations: 60 ml from the can, into the sauce (s1)

canonicalIngredients.name: oil for frying
observations: neutral oil 1.5 cm deep in pan, reused after (s1)
vegetable oil for deep-fry, or 1 cm shallow-fry (s2)

causalSequence: cube pork 2-3 cm; marinate with soy/salt, egg, seasoning 15-20 min
stir sauce: ketchup, sugar, vinegar, water (+ soy or pineapple juice); set aside
chop capsicum, onion, pineapple into bite-size chunks
fry pork in batches 5-8 min until golden and cooked through; drain on paper towel
stir-fry capsicum and onion 1-3 min until crisp-charred; add pineapple briefly
pour in sauce; bubble 1-2 min until thick and glossy
return pork, toss to coat; serve immediately over rice
techniqueFacts: cut is unanimous: pork shoulder / scotch fillet (butt) — fat keeps it juicy; lean loin or tenderloin dries out (s1, s2 warn explicitly)
all three velvet the pork: egg-based marinade 15-20 min; s1 adds 1/4 tsp bicarb for restaurant-soft texture (optional), s2 uses egg white only
coating is cornflour-led everywhere; s0 layers plain flour first then cornstarch
double-fry is the restaurant crunch lever (s0: 150-175 C 7-8 min then 200 C 1-2 min; s2: 350 F then 1 min refry)

single shallow pan-fry is a sanctioned home path: s1 fries once in 1.5 cm oil 5-6 min per batch and notes the sauce softens the coating anyway; s2 endorses ~1 cm shallow-fry with thinner pieces; s2 tested baking and rejects it (dry, not crispy)

sauce base is ketchup + sugar + vinegar in all three; acid varies (white / apple cider / rice wine); s1 says cut vinegar to 60 ml for a sweeter sauce; s2 adds worcestershire for depth and skips cornflour (ketchup body is enough)
veg stays crisp: 30 s in the wok (s0) up to 2-3 min (s2); pineapple always added after the veg, briefly
s1 uses canned pineapple in juice (never syrup) and puts the reserved juice in the sauce; s2 argues fresh pineapple caramelises better
serve immediately — the coating soaks sauce and softens within minutes (all three)
s1 is the speed benchmark: 35 min total, one pan; also gives a 200 C air-fryer variant, 8-10 min flipping halfway
high-smoke-point neutral oil only (corn, canola, vegetable, peanut); olive oil warned against (s0, s2)
